title: IBM poised for modest third-quarter beat, says Bank of America
detail:
IBM poised for modest third-quarter beat, says Bank of America

IBM
BAC
Explore stocks on Coinbase

IBM poised for modest third-quarter beat, says Bank of America Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Bank of America expects International Business Machines Corp (NYSE:IBM), the technology and consulting group, to deliver a modest third-quarter earnings beat on October 21 while keeping its financial 2026 outlook unchanged.

The bank reiterated its 'buy' rating and $280 price target, citing IBM's shift towards higher-margin software, improving profitability and strong free cash flow.

Bank of America forecasts third-quarter revenue of $16.8 billion and earnings per share of $2.82, with the potential for a slightly stronger performance from favourable currency movements and profitability.

The bank expects investors to focus on progress in converting delayed deals, signs of a recovery in customer spending and improving growth in Transaction Processing software.

Software growth remains below ideal levels, although Bank of America expects strength in Red Hat (NYSE:RHT)'s OpenShift and Ansible products, alongside continued expansion in the data business following IBM's acquisition of Confluent.

The bank forecasts 4.5% reported software growth for financial 2026, with organic growth, excluding acquisitions, expected to reach 1% for the year as Transaction Processing recovers gradually.

Infrastructure revenue is expected to grow 3% at constant exchange rates in the third quarter, while consulting revenue is forecast to rise 3.6% as growth improves in the second half.

Bank of America describes 2026 as a transitional year for IBM, with a stronger operating performance expected in 2027 as software growth and margins improve.

The bank trimmed its financial 2026 revenue forecast to $70.3 billion from $70.5 billion and its earnings-per-share estimate to $12.40 from $12.45, leaving its price target unchanged at $280.

Its valuation assumes IBM will trade at 19 times the estimated 2027 enterprise value to free cash flow, a measure comparing the company's overall value with the cash it generates after operating costs and capital expenditure.

title: What Changed For Dell Stock, And What Did Not?
detail:
What Changed For Dell Stock, And What Did Not?
Trefis Team

Dell Technologies (DELL) stock fell 11.3% on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, far more than the 1.1% decline for the S&P 500. The slide followed a downgrade earlier that day from Barclays, which lowered the shares to Equal Weight from Overweight amid concerns that enterprise AI adoption is lagging. While the analysts worry about timing, the computer maker has maintained a rapid clip. So how big is the part of Dell that has been doing the growing?

Infrastructure Overtook Dell's Client Segment In Fiscal 2026

Dell's Infrastructure Solutions Group brought in $60.8 billion in fiscal 2026, which ended in January 2026. That division generated 53.6% of company revenue, with its revenue expanding 39.5% from the year before. Meanwhile, the Client Solutions Group, the other main business segment at Dell, grew 5.4% to $51.0 billion.

The balance of power looked completely different just a year earlier. Back then, the client business was the larger of the two, accounting for 50.6% of revenue against 45.6% for infrastructure. Over a single year, infrastructure leaped from the smaller segment to representing more than half of Dell. The infrastructure business is the part of the company expanding at speed, whereas the client operations have grown slowly.

What Dell Stock Costs Now

Even after Wednesday's drop, Dell trades at 28.8 times its earnings over the past twelve months, compared with 22.7 times for the S&P 500. Investors are paying that premium for growth. During the three months to July 2026, or fiscal Q2 2027, Dell's revenue rose 57.7% from a year earlier.

That blistering pace is a recent development for Dell. Revenue over the past twelve months grew 49.0%, a sharp acceleration from the 10.5% rate seen in the twelve months before.

Dell's Profits Are Where They Were Before Wednesday

Wednesday's market action changed the price of Dell stock, but it changed nothing about the profit the company has already reported for its latest quarter and past year. Dell posted an operating margin of 11.6% in fiscal Q2 2027, up from 6.4% in the same quarter a year earlier. Over the past twelve months, net income reached $11.4 billion, more than double the $4.84 billion recorded in the twelve months before.

The operating margin over the past twelve months stood at 9.6%, its highest at any quarter-end in data going back to fiscal Q3 2017. This metric is the number to watch in the company's next report, expected on or around November 23, 2026. The margin reveals whether Dell's faster revenue growth is still translating into higher profit.

title: Should You Trim Or Add To Your RGTI Stock Position Now?

Rigetti Computing (RGTI) stock lost 78.7% over the past year, even as the S&P 500 returned 17.3%. The underlying business moved in the opposite direction. Revenue for April to June 2026 reached $5.14 million, up 185.3% from a year earlier. Shareholders watching sales climb while the stock sinks face a genuine choice about whether to trim or add to their positions. So what are buyers paying for Rigetti today?

What Rigetti Buyers Get For Their Money

Rigetti stock trades at 291.5 times its sales over the twelve months to June 2026. The S&P 500 trades at 3.1 times sales by comparison. This multiple reflects a market value of about $3.9 billion set against revenue of $13.4 million. A traditional price-to-earnings ratio offers no insight here, as Rigetti lost money over those twelve months.

The company also loses money on its operations. Its operating loss over the same twelve months equaled 727.6% of its revenue. By contrast, the S&P 500 as a whole kept 18.5% of its revenue as operating profit. Anyone buying the stock at today's price appears to be paying for sales well beyond what Rigetti reports now.

This recent jump in sales follows two years of shrinking revenue, which included a 37.2% drop over the twelve months to June 2025. Across its last three twelve-month periods, Rigetti posted average revenue growth of 6.3%, close to the 5.9% average for the S&P 500. That average blends two drops with a 68.5% jump, so it hides far bigger swings than the index shows. Rigetti would have to grow far faster than that historical pace to bring its sales multiple anywhere near the broader market.

Is Rigetti Losing Less Money As It Grows?

In dollar terms, the answer is not yet. Rigetti saw its operating loss for April to June 2026 grow to $28.1 million, up from $19.9 million a year earlier. Revenue grew faster, shrinking the loss to 546.2% of revenue from 1,104%. According to an August 7 news report, the quarter's revenue beat estimates but its earnings missed them. The report blamed higher R&D and SG&A costs. For anyone adding shares, that is the risk: the company is spending more as it grows, and its loss has grown too.

Rigetti can afford to carry those losses for now. The company held $394 million in cash and short-term investments on June 30, 2026, against total debt of $7.7 million. Its free cash outflow over the twelve months to June 2026 was $87.6 million. At that pace, the existing cash balance would cover about four and a half years. That pace is rising, however. The outflow of $27.8 million for April to June 2026 was the largest of the past five quarters. At that quarter's pace, the cash would last about three and a half years.

title: How Much Downside Is Left In QBTS Stock?

How Much Downside Is Left In QBTS Stock?

Shares of D-Wave Quantum (QBTS) lost 21.0% in the week to October 14, 2026. The S&P 500 posted a 1.0% dip over the same period. The drop left D-Wave shares closing at their lowest point of the past year, finishing 73.1% below their highest level. When the whole market has turned down before, how far did D-Wave fall, and how long did it take to come back?

D-Wave Drawdown Was Over Four Times Greater Than The Benchmark

D-Wave stock has traded through five market shocks since August 2022, falling 51.2% on average during those events. That decline is about four and a half times the S&P 500's average fall of 11.3%. The company experienced its deepest drop during the 2023 yield shock, losing 73.0% while the S&P 500 lost 9.5%. D-Wave also fell 61.0% in the 2022 inflation shock.

Across all five shocks, the median recovery from a low back to the previous peak took 3.0 months. Investors waited more than a year to recover from those two falls. The stock required 12.9 months to climb back after the 2023 yield shock. Following the 2022 inflation shock, the shares took 30.7 months to return to their prior highs, recovering in May 2025.

Operating Deficit Doubled At D-Wave In A Year

D-Wave reported $3.08 million in revenue during the April to June 2026 quarter, remaining about level with the same period a year earlier. Over the twelve months ending in June 2026, revenue fell 44.2% compared to the prior twelve-month span. System sales represented the majority of the company's 2025 revenue, generating $16.2 million out of a total $24.6 million. The smaller Quantum Computing as a Service (QCaaS) business shrank 18.2% that year.

During the April to June quarter, D-Wave posted an operating loss of $53.3 million, doubling its deficit from a year earlier. The company held $546 million in cash and short-term investments at the end of June 2026, down from the $819 million it reported the previous year. This cash reserve remains large compared to the company's $48.1 million in debt.

D-Wave Missed Estimates But Grew Its Backlog

On August 6, D-Wave reported a loss of $0.10 a share for its fiscal second quarter of 2026. This deficit was wider than the $0.08 loss analysts had expected. It was still narrower than the company's $0.55 loss a year earlier.

D-Wave ended June with $40.7 million of signed-contract backlog. It expects about $23.2 million of that to become revenue within 12 months, and $29.3 million within two years.

Does This Mean You Should Act On QBTS?

Our purpose is to inform you with unique data so you make the right investment decisions. That said, betting on a single stock is always risky, no matter which direction you choose.

title: Here's What a $10,000 Investment in IonQ Could Be Worth by October 2027
detail:
Here's What a $10,000 Investment in IonQ Could Be Worth by October 2027

Though the technology is still in its early days, advancements in quantum computing are starting to pick up steam. Microsoft unveiled a new quantum chip in June and says it expects to build a scalable quantum computer by 2029. IBM is also working on a large-scale quantum computer, Quantum Starling, and plans to unveil it in 2029. Not to be left out, Alphabet and Amazon are also working on quantum chips.

Outside those tech giants, however, sit a number of much smaller pure-play quantum computing companies that investors may find intriguing.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

One of these is IonQ (NYSE: IONQ). Founded in 2015, it focuses entirely on quantum-related areas, including computing, networking, and security.

The stock hasn't performed well over the last 12 months, however, having dropped 57% as of this writing -- dropping its market cap to just $13.8 billion -- while the S&P 500 rose 17% over the same period. Also, with a beta of 3.3, the IonQ stock price generally experiences swings that are 3.3 times as large as the broader market.

That said, based on analysts' one-year forecasts, by October 2027, the stock's trend line could have quite the reversal from the declines it has experienced over the past 12 months.

Image source: The Motley Fool.
The outlook for the IonQ stock price

Analysts have a generally favorable opinion of the stock. According to CNN, of the 16 who cover it, 13 rate it as a buy, while three rate it as a hold. From that group, the median one-year price target is $65. On Oct. 13, its opening price was $35.82, so if it hits that target, a $10,000 investment will be worth approximately $18,146.

Looking at some other scenarios, the highest price target among those analysts is $100, which would turn $10,000 into $27,917. And even hitting the lowest price target of $49 would grow a $10,000 investment into a position worth about $13,679.

Investment considerations

Price targets, of course, aren't perfect predictions. All of those analysts could be wrong, and one year from now, IonQ's stock price could be flat or lower than it is today. What those targets do offer, however, is a sentiment gauge that investors can use to help establish a risk-to-reward framework as a part of their decision-making process.

Quantum computing may still be a few years away from being ready for more mainstream adoption in the business world, but the fact that big tech players like Alphabet, Amazon, IBM, and Microsoft have all gotten involved in the space shows that it has the potential to be more than a niche market. IonQ is currently seeing some of that momentum in its earnings results. In the second quarter, it reported $80.1 million in revenue, a 287% increase compared to the prior-year period. In that quarterly report, it also announced it was boosting its full-year revenue guidance from a $260 million to $270 million range to a $280 million to $290 million range.

title: Siemens joins IBM research effort to develop nanostack technology
detail:
Siemens joins IBM research effort to develop nanostack technology
IBM's nanostack architecture vertically stacks nanosheet-based transistors in three dimensions · Verdict · Rene1208/Shutterstock.com.
BV Swagath
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:09 AM PDT 3 min read
IBM
SIE.DE
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

IBM and Siemens have entered a research collaboration aimed at advancing nanostack, the chip maker's three-dimensional transistor architecture capable of packing nearly 100 billion transistors onto a fingernail-sized chip.

The partnership brings together IBM's semiconductor device research and Siemens' capabilities in electronic design automation (EDA), process simulation, lithography optimisation, and advanced manufacturing software. Their joint objective is to compress development timelines and build the manufacturing groundwork required to move nanostack toward commercial production.

Described by IBM as the industry's first known 3D nanosheet-based transistor design, nanostack vertically stacks and staggers transistors to achieve far greater density than conventional planar approaches. At its current 7 angstrom node, the architecture achieves nearly two times the transistor density per unit area compared with the nanosheet technology behind IBM's 2nm chips, which were introduced in 2021.

The approach marks a departure from more than 60 years of semiconductor scaling that operated exclusively along the X and Y axes. By building upward on a given chip footprint, nanostack unlocks the Z axis for density gains.

IBM has drawn an analogy with high-density urban construction, where vertical building on a fixed plot yields significantly more usable space.

Engineers can also use different material combinations within each vertically stacked layer, making it possible to tune performance and power consumption for individual transistors without affecting others in the stack. IBM has said these capabilities deliver substantial gains in energy efficiency, overall performance, and SRAM scaling.

IBM silicon technology research and development (R&D) vice president Huiming Bu said: "Nanostack is a scalable transistor platform designed to shift device scaling from 2D to 3D, representing a new paradigm for the semiconductor industry and a path forward for the logic scaling needed to support AI and other emerging technologies over the coming decade."

Although IBM demonstrated the viability of the architecture earlier this year, significant further development is needed before it can be manufactured at scale.

The collaboration will centre on creating advanced virtual models of nanostack devices, enabling the two companies to simulate performance, refine designs, and identify potential fabrication obstacles before physical chips are produced.

Work will also target the design, simulation, and lithography techniques required for future nanostack generations beyond the 7 angstrom node.

Heading into today, shares of the technology and consulting company had lost 7.08% over the past month, lagging the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 3.49% and the S&P 500's gain of 2.06%.

In terms of the entire fiscal year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates predict earnings of $12.33 per share and a revenue of $70.42 billion, indicating changes of +6.38% and +4.27%, respectively, from the former year.

It is also important to note the recent changes to analyst estimates for IBM. These recent revisions tend to reflect the evolving nature of short-term business trends. As a result, we can interpret positive estimate revisions as a good sign for the business outlook.

Empirical research indicates that these revisions in estimates have a direct correlation with impending stock price performance. To take advantage of this, we've established the Zacks Rank, an exclusive model that considers these estimated changes and delivers an operational rating system.

The Zacks Rank system ranges from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell). It has a remarkable, outside-audited track record of success, with #1 stocks delivering an average annual return of +25% since 1988. Over the past month, the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate has shifted 0.04% upward. IBM is currently a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

From a valuation perspective, IBM is currently exchanging hands at a Forward P/E ratio of 18.71. This valuation marks a discount compared to its industry average Forward P/E of 19.71.

We can additionally observe that IBM currently boasts a PEG ratio of 2.2. The PEG ratio is similar to the widely-used P/E ratio, but this metric also takes the company's expected earnings growth rate into account.
